transcript: Last night, I saw Robert Downey Jr in the title role of McNeal at Lincoln Center. This is a new play by Ayad Akhtar who wrote the Pulitzer Prize winning play Disgraced about a decade ago. Unlike that play, McNeal unfortunately did not impress me. Making his Broadway debut, Robert Downey Jr plays a writer who, despite being very successful, has a slew of problems including but not limited to excessive drinking, a strained relationship with his son, and a concerning level of arrogance. Although it has solid performances from the entire cast, I found the writing to be very plain and the plot and themes rather unfocused. AI and its role in writing and debates about what truth is seems to be a prominent theme but it's pretty much overshadowed by a rather uninteresting plot. The stagecraft is pretty impressive though and again the acting was good, so if the themes interest you then you very well may enjoy this, it was just not for me. With that, another playbill for my collection.
